title: PMP: Pattern Morphing-based Memory Partitioning in High-Level Synthesis
problem: Memory partitioning in high-level synthesis is constrained by fixed access pattern shapes, leading to sub-optimal bank numbers or excessive address generation overhead. Previous hyperplane-based methods cannot flexibly adapt to varying data access patterns.
motivation: Reducing memory access conflicts and improving FPGA resource utilization through more effective memory partitioning strategies in automated hardware synthesis.
method: PMP reshapes how data is accessed in memory—a technique called pattern morphing—to reduce the number of separate memory banks the hardware needs. Rather than being stuck with one fixed access pattern, it transforms the pattern into different mathematically equivalent shapes using reduced hyperplane families, giving it flexibility that older methods lacked. The approach then solves an optimization problem (integer linear programming) to find the reshaping that minimizes wasted space (data padding overhead). This adaptive strategy replaces the rigid, one-size-fits-all patterns that previous hyperplane-based methods required.
key_novelty: By combining pattern morphing with integer linear programming optimization, the approach automatically finds the minimum number of memory banks needed for any data access pattern, rather than being constrained by the pattern's original shape.
contributions: Pattern morphing-based memory partitioning technique for HLS
ILP formulation to minimize data padding overhead
Optimal partition factor determination without pattern shape restrictions
Average 22% LUT, 21% FlipFlop, 10% DSP, and 40% memory overhead reduction versus prior methods
primary_theme: Memory partitioning optimization for FPGA synthesis
